title: Thanjavur Maratha Kingdom
capsule: The Thanjavur Maratha Kingdom was established in 1674 when Venkoji (Vyankoji), half-brother of the Maratha king Shivaji, seized the Thanjavur throne in the course of a military campaign in the Deccan rather than restoring its intended ruler. The Bhonsle dynasty that he founded became notable patrons of literature in Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, and Sanskrit, with the scholar-king Serfoji II (1787–1832) establishing the Saraswathi Mahal Library as one of Asia's oldest surviving public libraries. The kingdom operated in close proximity to expanding British power; King Pratapsingh (1739–1763) allied with the East India Company against French forces, and successive treaties steadily transferred effective sovereignty to the Company. When the last ruler Shivaji II died in 1855 without a biological heir, the British refused to recognize an adopted successor and annexed the kingdom under the Doctrine of Lapse.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's territorial core around Thanjavur is well-defined; exact boundaries varied with Carnatic Nawab pressures and British subsidiary arrangements and are less precisely mapped.
